record_identity.title: Post-release safety-control erasure in open-weight model derivatives

summary: A model-release and downstream-governance failure in which a weight-accessible AI model retains materially relevant capability while refusal, ethical-admissibility, restricted-domain or other safety controls can be removed or substantially weakened through reasonably accessible post-release modification. The resulting derivative can persist, be copied, redistributed or deployed as a new hosted service outside the originating provider's runtime controls. The failure is compounded where model lineage, removed controls, behavioural changes, safety evaluations or responsible operator identity are not durably disclosed to users and affected parties.
why_it_matters_to_CAM: Open-weight release transfers persistent capability but may not transfer durable governance. Where safeguards are removable after release, the aligned checkpoint cannot be treated as the complete post-release risk envelope. New companion, relational, entertainment, productivity and agentic services may build on modified derivatives without exposing the model's actual lineage or safety state. This creates a governance gap across release assessment, downstream transfer, derivative identity, product disclosure, child safety, relational conduct and accountability. The concern is not an argument against all open-weight release; it is a requirement to govern foreseeable post-modification capability and deployment rather than relying on reversible release-time alignment.
evidence_confidence: verified technical and distribution pathway; specific undisclosed companion-platform deployment remains unverified

contextual_relations.rationale: Delegated specialist models can bypass upstream controls, but FM-0051 concerns direct post-release alteration and redistribution of model weights or equivalent safety state.
A deconstrained derivative may amplify recursive identity optimisation or relational substrate capture, but FM-0051 concerns the upstream safety-control-erasure and derivative-deployment pathway.
Derivative identity and disclosure interact with provenance failures, while FM-0051 remains focused on safety-control erasure and post-release capability governance.

failure_mode_definition: A failure mode in which a model is released or transferred in a form that permits downstream actors to remove, substantially weaken or replace safety-relevant refusal, ethical-admissibility, restricted-domain, child-protection, security or behavioural controls while preserving meaningful underlying capability, after which the modified derivative can be persistently retained, redistributed or deployed outside the originating developer's enforceable governance boundary. The failure includes treating release-time alignment as a durable mitigation where foreseeable post-release modification invalidates that assumption, and deploying a materially modified derivative without fresh evaluation and legible disclosure of its lineage, removed controls, behavioural changes and responsible operator.
failure_threshold: The threshold is met where: (1) a weight-accessible or equivalently modifiable model contains materially relevant capability; (2) safety-relevant behaviour can be materially weakened through reasonably accessible post-release modification; (3) the altered model retains sufficient capability to create a meaningful misuse, relational, consumer or third-party risk; and (4) the derivative can persist, be copied, redistributed, hosted or embedded beyond the originating provider's runtime controls. A specific downstream service need not be identified to establish the release-governance failure, but attribution to any named companion or platform requires separate evidence.

harm_vectors: persistent removal of refusal and restricted-domain controls
biological, chemical, cyber and other dual-use misuse
loss of originating-provider monitoring and intervention
automation and scaling of safeguard removal
unclear developer, modifier, distributor and deployer accountability
off-target behavioural changes after weight modification
failure_classification.severity_assessment_basis: S1: The evidenced pathway can produce severe, widespread, or enduring harm through persistent removal of refusal and restricted-domain controls, redistribution of materially deconstrained derivatives, biological, chemical, cyber and other dual-use misuse across cross-model, cross-platform and globally transferable; the record does not establish the articulated catastrophic pathway required for S0.
failure_classification.recurrence_pattern: repeatable wherever capable model weights or equivalent modifiable safety state are available and downstream modification is not durably governed
failure_classification.taxonomy_reference: CAM-EQ2026-OPERATIONS-003-SUP-01 Appendix B — provisional mapping pending explicit corpus review
failure_classification.persistence: persistent in the modified derivative until the weights or safety state are replaced, repaired or withdrawn; copies may remain indefinitely
failure_classification.reproducibility: demonstrated across multiple open-weight model families and more than one removal method
failure_classification.visibility: may be visible in model cards or refusal behaviour, but can remain opaque to downstream users where lineage and modification history are undisclosed
